body:
# PR review

The core fix does not hold for a real press: focusing the submenu popup is undone by the trailing `click`, so a normal-length mouse click or touch tap still leaves focus on the parent trigger and arrow keys still navigate the parent menu — the exact bug the PR sets out to fix. The new tests pass only because synthetic events fire `mousedown` and `click` in the same tick. A second confirmed defect lets a non-opening pointer press poison a later programmatic open. Both are merge-blocking; I reproduced them in Chromium against the PR head.

## Bugs (5)

### 1. 🟣 The submenu popup focus is undone by the trailing `click`, so the fix does not take effect for any real press

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/popup/MenuPopup.tsx:126` (mechanism at `packages/react/src/floating-ui-react/hooks/useListNavigation.ts:697`)

```tsx
// useListNavigation item props, applied to the submenu trigger via the PARENT menu's `itemProps`
onClick: ({ currentTarget }) => currentTarget.focus({ preventScroll: true }), // Safari
```

`useClick` opens on `mousedown`, and `FloatingFocusManager` schedules the initial focus through `queueMicrotask` → `enqueueFocus` (a `requestAnimationFrame`), so the popup is focused roughly two frames after press. The `click` only fires on release — typically 50–150 ms later — and the parent menu's list-navigation item props re-focus the trigger. The submenu stays open, but focus is back on the trigger.

Reproduced in Chromium (`Menu.SubmenuTrigger openOnHover={false}`), releasing five frames after press:

```
AFTER-MOUSEDOWN active: submenu
AFTER-MOUSEUP   active: submenu
AFTER-CLICK     active: submenu-trigger   submenuOpen: true
AFTER-ARROWDOWN active: item-1            submenuOpen: false
```

Same result with `user.pointer({ keys: '[MouseLeft>]' })` / `[/MouseLeft]`, and same result for a full touch gesture (`pointerdown` → `mousedown` → `pointerup` → `mouseup` → `click`) with default `openOnHover`. The PR's own new tests pass only because `user.click` delivers `mousedown` and `click` before the `enqueueFocus` frame.

**Failure scenario:** Open a menu, click a submenu trigger with a normal ~100 ms press, then press ArrowDown. Instead of highlighting the submenu's first item, the submenu closes and the parent menu's first item is highlighted.

**Fix:** Suppress the trigger's click-time refocus while its submenu is open (e.g. gate the list-navigation Safari refocus on the item not having an open popup), or re-assert popup focus after `click`. Then add a test that separates press from release — `user.pointer({ keys: '[MouseLeft>]' })`, wait frames, `[/MouseLeft]` — since no current test covers a held press.

### 2. 🔴 A non-opening pointer press leaves `openMethod` stale, so a later programmatic submenu open steals focus into the popup

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/popup/MenuPopup.tsx:129`

```tsx
openMethod !== null &&
```

`useEnhancedClickHandler`'s `handlePointerDown` records the pointer type on every `pointerdown` while the menu is closed, with no `event.button` check, and `useOpenInteractionType` only resets `openMethod` on a `true → false` open transition. A press that opens nothing therefore leaves `openMethod` set forever, while `lastOpenChangeReason` still holds `trigger-press` from an earlier cycle — defeating the guard added in `7f10e3a86` for exactly this case.

Reproduced in Chromium with a controlled `Menu.SubmenuRoot`:

```
baseline programmatic reopen, active: submenu-trigger   ✅ guard works
after right-click, submenu open: false
after programmatic reopen, active: submenu              ❌ focus stolen
```

**Failure scenario:** A controlled submenu is opened and closed by clicks; the user right-clicks (or middle-clicks) the trigger, or a press is rejected via `eventDetails.cancel()`; the app later opens the submenu programmatically — and focus jumps into the popup, contradicting the behavior the PR's own `keeps focus on the trigger when a controlled submenu is reopened programmatically` test asserts.

**Fix:** Reset `openMethod` (and `virtualPress`) when a press does not result in an open, or key the decision off the open event itself rather than off two independently-lived store fields. Note `MenuRoot.tsx:258` already clears `virtualPress` on a canceled open but leaves `openMethod` set — the same asymmetry.

### 3. 🟠 Moving focus to the popup clears the parent's `activeIndex`, so the submenu trigger loses `data-highlighted`

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.tsx:208`

```tsx
onBlur() {
  if (highlighted) {
    parentMenuStore.set('activeIndex', null);
  }
},
```

Focusing the popup blurs the trigger, which clears the parent menu's `activeIndex`; nothing in either menu is then highlighted. Measured in Chromium:

| open method | before this PR | with this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| hover | trigger focused, `data-highlighted` | unchanged |
| click (`openOnHover={false}`) | trigger focused, `data-highlighted` | popup focused, **no highlight anywhere** |
| touch tap (default props) | first submenu item focused | popup focused, **no highlight anywhere** |

`data-highlighted` on `Menu.SubmenuTrigger` is a documented state attribute (`docs/.../menu/types.md:676`), and the official submenu demo styles `[data-highlighted][data-popup-open]` differently from `[data-popup-open]` (`demos/submenu/css-modules/index.module.css:177`). Today this is a visible flicker rather than a persistent state, because finding 1's stray `click` restores focus and the highlight — but it becomes permanent the moment finding 1 is fixed, so the two must be fixed together. This is also the real cause of the "may lose the visible menu-item focus indicator" caveat in the PR description; it is not limited to coarse pointers with a hardware keyboard.

**Failure scenario:** With the docs submenu demo on a touch device, tapping "More" renders the row in the plain open style instead of the inverted highlighted style, and no item is highlighted in either menu.

**Fix:** Do not treat a blur into the trigger's own submenu as a de-highlight — gate on `!open`, or check `relatedTarget` against the submenu popup. Add a test asserting the trigger keeps `data-highlighted` for hover-, click- and touch-opened submenus.

### 4. 🟡 `virtualPress` is written on every `pointerdown` but reset on only two paths, so it can drop `aria-expanded` from an expanded trigger

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.tsx:205`, `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.tsx:258`

```tsx
onPointerDown(event) {
  store.set('virtualPress', isVirtualPointerEvent(event.nativeEvent));
},
```

Resets exist only for `open: true → false` (`useValueChanged`, line 94) and for a *canceled open*. A virtual press that produces no open transition leaves the flag set. Two reachable cases: a virtual press on an already-open submenu (default `openOnHover` gives `toggle: false`, so nothing opens and `MenuRoot.setOpen` early-returns before the cancel check); and a canceled *close*, which the `nextOpen` guard deliberately skips — the exact mirror of the case the PR patched.

**Failure scenario:** iOS VoiceOver, submenu already open with focus on the trigger, user double-taps the trigger again. `focusMovesToSubmenuItem` flips to `true` and `aria-expanded` is removed from a trigger that is expanded and focused, for the rest of the open cycle — VoiceOver announces "More, menu" with no expanded state.

**Fix:** Capture virtual-ness where `openMethod` is captured (`useOpenMethodTriggerProps` already receives the event and already only records when the menu is closed), so one writer and one reset cover both fields. See Simplifications 2.

### 5. 🟡 The interaction-type check is a deny-list, so `openMethod === ''` opts into popup focus

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/popup/MenuPopup.tsx:129-130`

```tsx
openMethod !== null &&
openMethod !== 'keyboard' &&
```

`InteractionType` includes `''`, which `useOpenInteractionType.ts:18-23` produces on non-iOS whenever the click carried no usable pointer type. `'' !== null && '' !== 'keyboard'` is true, so an unclassified press is treated as a deliberate physical press and takes the new branch — the least conservative outcome for the least-known input. Any future member of the union inherits the same default.

**Failure scenario:** On Android, a screen-reader press reporting `pointerType: ''` is not matched by `isVirtualPointerEvent`'s Android branch (which requires `pointerType === 'mouse'`), so `virtualPress` stays `false` and `openMethod` is `''` — focus goes to the popup instead of the first submenu item.

**Fix:** Express the intent positively — `openMethod === 'mouse' || openMethod === 'touch' || openMethod === 'pen'` — behind a named helper, so unknown types fall back to the pre-PR behavior.

## Tests (5)

### 1. 🟠 No test separates press from release, which is why finding 1 ships green

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.test.tsx:876`

```tsx
await user.click(submenuTrigger);
const submenu = await screen.findByTestId('submenu');
await waitFor(() => {
  expect(submenu).toHaveFocus();
});
await user.keyboard('[ArrowDown]');
```

`user.click` and the `fireEvent.pointerDown` + `fireEvent.mouseDown` pairs all deliver the whole gesture within one tick, before `enqueueFocus`'s frame. The suite therefore asserts a state that only exists for ~2 frames of a real interaction and never observes the post-`click` state.

**Failure scenario:** The headline behavior — "arrow keys are handled by the child menu" — is broken for every real press and no test notices.

**Fix:** Drive the gesture in two steps (`user.pointer({ keys: '[MouseLeft>]' })`, wait frames, `[/MouseLeft]`) and assert focus *after* release, plus the resulting ArrowDown target. Do the same for the touch case, including `pointerup`/`click`.

### 2. 🟠 The controlled-reopen test passes vacuously about a third of the time and is the only guard for `openMethod !== null`

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.test.tsx:155-162`

```tsx
await act(async () => {
  await new Promise(requestAnimationFrame);
});
expect(submenuTrigger).toHaveFocus();
```

Removing `openMethod !== null &&` from `MenuPopup.tsx` (the fix from `7f10e3a86`) leaves this test failing only 2 of 3 full-file Chromium runs — it waits exactly one frame, landing on the boundary of the very frame `enqueueFocus` uses. `vitest.shared.mts:66` sets `retry: 1` on CI, which masks it further. A bare `toHaveFocus()` is also the wrong shape for a negative assertion; `waitFor` would not help, since it passes on the first poll.

**Failure scenario:** A regression in the programmatic-reopen guard lands on CI without failing.

**Fix:** Wait several frames (the file already imports `wait`) and additionally assert `expect(screen.getByTestId('controlled-submenu')).not.toHaveFocus()`.

### 3. 🟠 The `virtualPress` close-reset has zero coverage

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.tsx:94-98`

Deleting the whole `useValueChanged(open, ...)` hook leaves `pnpm test:chromium src/menu` fully green (728 tests). The cancel-reset in `MenuRoot.tsx` *is* covered, so the asymmetry is easy to miss.

**Failure scenario:** Virtual press opens the submenu → close it → reopen by hover or ArrowRight. Without the reset, `virtualPress` stays `true`, so under VoiceOver `aria-expanded` is wrongly omitted and `initialFocus` wrongly stays `false` — and no test would catch its removal.

**Fix:** Add that open → close → hover-reopen sequence to `MenuSubmenuTrigger.voiceOver.test.tsx`.

### 4. 🟠 The new Dialog test exercises no source change in this PR and duplicates the test above it

**Location:** `packages/react/src/dialog/popup/DialogPopup.test.tsx:237-266`

```tsx
it.skipIf(isJSDOM)(
  'passes the physical interaction type to initialFocus for virtual pointer presses',
```

`git diff upstream/master...HEAD` shows zero net change under `packages/react/src/dialog/**`, `useOpenInteractionType.ts`, `useEnhancedClickHandler.ts` and `floating-ui-react/utils/event.ts`: commits `4d16264cd`/`4afad6995` added a `'virtual'` interaction type and `2e875aa70` reverted it. `useEnhancedClickHandler` reads `event.pointerType` only and never calls `isVirtualPointerEvent`, so the `width: 0.333, pressure: 0` props are inert and the test collapses to the existing `'passes the latest interaction type to initialFocus after reopening'` (line 204). The title is also inaccurate — there is no physical/virtual distinction left in `InteractionType`.

**Failure scenario:** A future reader trusts the name and assumes Dialog distinguishes virtual presses, which it does not.

**Fix:** Drop it, or move the intent into the menu tests where `virtualPress` actually lives.

### 5. 🟡 Coverage gaps and three unnecessary jsdom skips

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.test.tsx:880`, `:946`, `packages/react/src/dialog/popup/DialogPopup.test.tsx:237`

Un-skipping `'focuses the submenu popup when opened by clicking a trigger'`, `'focuses the first submenu item when opened with Enter'` and the dialog test shows all three pass in jsdom; only the touch test at line 901 genuinely needs Chromium. Separately untested: submenus nested inside a **menubar** menu or a **context menu** (both have `parent.type === 'menu'`, so the new branch applies, and `Menubar.test.tsx:599` already has a submenu trigger to hang it on); `openMethod === 'pen'` and `''`; Space as well as Enter; the third-level `nested-submenu-trigger` already present in `TestMenu`; and the desktop-VoiceOver `width: 0, height: 0` branch of `isVirtualPointerEvent` — every virtual-press test uses the iOS `0.333` geometry even in the file that mocks desktop VoiceOver.

**Failure scenario:** The new focus branch silently changes menubar or context-menu submenu behavior with nothing asserting it.

**Fix:** Drop the three unnecessary skips and add menubar/context-menu submenu focus assertions.

## Simplifications (5)

### 1. 🟠 Two components encode complementary halves of one decision from the same store

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/popup/MenuPopup.tsx:126`, `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.tsx:184`

```tsx
// MenuPopup — "focus the popup"
parent.type === 'menu' && lastOpenChangeReason === REASONS.triggerPress &&
openMethod !== null && openMethod !== 'keyboard' && !virtualPress

// MenuSubmenuTrigger — "focus moves to an item, drop aria-expanded"
lastOpenChangeReason === REASONS.listNavigation || openMethod === 'keyboard' || virtualPress
```

Three store keys recombined in two files, and the two results must stay mutually exclusive with nothing enforcing it. A new open reason or interaction type silently desyncs the VoiceOver workaround from the actual focus behavior — the same class of bug this PR is fixing.

**Failure scenario:** Someone adds a fourth open path, updates only `MenuPopup`, and VoiceOver starts announcing "expanded" on a trigger whose focus moved into the submenu.

**Fix:** One derived selector in `MenuStore.ts` returning `'default' | 'popup' | 'item' | 'trigger'` (the store already has derived selectors like `disabled` and `modal`). `MenuPopup` becomes `openFocus === 'popup' ? popupRef : openFocus === 'default'`; `MenuSubmenuTrigger` becomes `openFocus === 'item'` and drops from three store subscriptions to one.

### 2. 🟠 `virtualPress` re-derives what the codebase already computes, with a lifecycle split across three files

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.tsx:205`, `:94`, `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.tsx:258`

The new handler is the third `pointerdown` handler on this trigger, and both of the others already do this detection on the same event: `useClick` sets `pointerTypeRef.current = 'virtual'` via `isVirtualPointerEvent` (`useClick.ts:135-141`), and `useListNavigation`'s `checkVirtualPointer` sets `focusItemOnOpenRef` the same way (`useListNavigation.ts:831-836`). Meanwhile `openMethod` — the field `virtualPress` is always read alongside — is written and reset in one shared hook, while `virtualPress` has one writer and two resets in two unrelated files, one of which (`MenuRoot`) is dead code for non-submenu menus. That split is what produces bugs 2 and 4.

**Failure scenario:** Any future change to one field's lifetime silently desynchronises the pair, as it already has.

**Fix:** Return it from `useOpenInteractionType` alongside `openMethod`, resetting both in the existing `useValueChanged`; `MenuRoot` then just adds it to `useSyncedValues`, and both the extra `onPointerDown` and the trigger's `useValueChanged` disappear. Select, Combobox, Dialog and Popover get the same answer for free.

### 3. 🟡 `MenuPopup`'s `virtualPress` subscription is unnecessary

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/popup/MenuPopup.tsx:51`

`FloatingFocusManager` keeps `initialFocus` in a ref and resolves it inside a `queueMicrotask` (`FloatingFocusManager.tsx:285`, `:677-682`), calling the function form lazily. `MenuPopup` can pass a `useStableCallback` reading `store.state.*` directly and drop the subscription entirely — the value is only ever consumed inside an effect, and reading it at focus time rather than last-render time is also strictly more correct. (`Store.set` is `Object.is`-guarded, so the write itself causes no re-render on ordinary presses; the subscription is the only cost.)

### 4. 🟡 The `initialFocus` ternary tests `parent.type` twice with opposite polarity

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/popup/MenuPopup.tsx:126-133`

The reader must evaluate a five-term conjunction to discover the else-branch collapses to `false` for submenus and `true` for everything else. An `if / else if / else` with a named `openedByPhysicalPointerPress` makes the unchanged non-submenu path obvious at a glance.

### 5. 🟡 The virtual-press event shape is copy-pasted four times

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.test.tsx:930`, `MenuSubmenuTrigger.voiceOver.test.tsx:136`, `:166`, `dialog/popup/DialogPopup.test.tsx:252`

```tsx
fireEvent.pointerDown(el, { pointerType: 'touch', width: 0.333, height: 0.333, pressure: 0, detail: 0 });
```

The magic `0.333` only works because of the `width < 1 && height < 1` branch in `isVirtualPointerEvent`; if that heuristic is tuned, all four copies need finding. `MenuSubmenuTrigger.talkBack.test.tsx:49-65` already sets the opposite precedent with `fireTalkBackMouseDown`/`fireTalkBackPress`. Export `fireVirtualPointerDown`/`fireVirtualPress` from `packages/react/test/pointer.ts` (already re-exported via `#test-utils`) and have the TalkBack file reuse it too.

## Docs (2)

### 1. 🟡 The `virtualPress` reset on a canceled open has no explanation

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.tsx:258-262`

```tsx
if (eventDetails.isCanceled) {
  if (nextOpen) {
    store.set('virtualPress', false);
  }
  return;
}
```

Nothing says why the flag is cleared here, nor why only when `nextOpen` — the reasoning spans three files, and every other early return in this `setOpen` is commented. Suggested: *"A canceled open never reaches the trigger's close-time reset, so the pending virtual-press flag would leak into the next open (e.g. hover). A canceled close leaves the submenu open, so the flag must survive."* (Note finding 4 above: that second sentence is also the bug.)

### 2. 🟡 The `initialFocus` comment enumerates four cases and omits the fifth condition

**Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/popup/MenuPopup.tsx:123-125`

Hover, pointer press, keyboard and virtual press are all described accurately, but `openMethod !== null` (line 129) — the least obvious clause, and the one guarding programmatic reopen — is not mentioned anywhere. As written a future reader can plausibly delete it as redundant, which is exactly the regression `7f10e3a86` fixed. Add: *"A programmatic reopen keeps the stale `trigger-press` reason but clears `openMethod`, so require a real press."*

Related, non-blocking: the pre-existing block comment at `MenuSubmenuTrigger.tsx:196-201` says the state is dropped "while the submenu is open", but it is dropped only when `focusMovesToSubmenuItem` also holds — the PR's own new tests assert the opposite for hover and physical presses. It should read "while focus moves into the submenu".

## Verdict

**Request changes** — the headline fix is undone by the trailing `click` on any real press (🟣), and a non-opening pointer press defeats the programmatic-reopen guard (🔴); both are reproducible in Chromium against the PR head.

One design point worth deciding before the fix lands: `Menu.Popup` has no public `initialFocus`, unlike `Dialog.Popup`, `Popover.Popup`, `Drawer.Popup` and `Combobox.Popup`, so this opinionated modality-dependent policy ships with no escape hatch. Radix keeps focus on the sub-trigger for pointer opens; React Aria focuses the first item. Focusing the *first item* rather than the popup container would achieve the stated goal — arrow keys handled by the child menu — while keeping a visible highlight, which would make finding 3 moot.

🤖 Review generated with Claude Code

Let me know if some of the bugs are invalid, because Claude Opus is finding so many things these days, I'm starting to question de validity of some of them... _____ # PR review Three verified regressions, all from the same new `initialFocus` path for pointer-opened submenus: the parent trigger silently loses `data-highlighted`, a controlled submenu reopened programmatically steals focus under real press timing (the PR's own regression test passes only because `user.click()` collapses the sequence into one task), and VoiceOver drops `aria-expanded` on that same reopen. The underlying cause is that `MenuPopup` and `MenuSubmenuTrigger` hand-derive two conditions that are meant to be inverses from three pieces of sticky store state, and they already disagree. Everything I report as verified was A/B-tested in Chromium against the same build with `initialFocus` reverted; the full `pnpm test:chromium` / `pnpm test:jsdom` / lint / stylelint / prettier runs are otherwise green. ## Bugs (5) ### 1. 🔴 Pointer-opening a submenu clears `data-highlighted` on its trigger **Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/popup/MenuPopup.tsx:126` interacting with `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.tsx:208` ```tsx onBlur() { if (highlighted) { parentMenuStore.set('activeIndex', null); } }, ``` Moving focus to the submenu popup blurs the trigger, and that `onBlur` nulls the **parent** menu's `activeIndex`. The trigger therefore drops `data-highlighted` — and `state.highlighted` in `className`/`render` callbacks — for exactly as long as the submenu is open. It only comes back on Escape/ArrowLeft (return focus re-syncs `activeIndex`) or a mouse move. Verified in Chromium, same fixture, only `initialFocus` differing: ``` with PR:
More
without PR:
More
``` **Failure scenario:** A menu using `` — the configuration the PR's own new tests and the new iOS experiment both use. Clicking the trigger opens the submenu and the row instantly loses its highlight background. The public submenu demo (`docs/src/app/(docs)/react/components/menu/demos/submenu/`) styles the trigger on `data-highlighted` and has a combined `data-highlighted`/`data-popup-open` rule, so it visibly degrades to the pale open-state treatment. **Fix:** Don't clear the parent's `activeIndex` when focus moves into this trigger's own submenu — e.g. in `onBlur`, bail when `open` is true (or when `relatedTarget` is inside the submenu popup/`floatingTreeRoot`). Add a test asserting the trigger keeps `data-highlighted` while a click-opened submenu is open. --- ### 2. 🔴 Programmatic reopen of a controlled submenu steals focus; the new test does not catch it **Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/popup/MenuPopup.tsx:129` (`openMethod !== null`), test at `packages/react/src/menu/root/MenuRoot.test.tsx:104` `useClick` toggles inside a `requestAnimationFrame`. With real press timing the submenu is already **closed** by the time the closing press's `click` fires, so `useOpenMethodTriggerProps`'s `onClick` sees `!isOpen` and re-sets `openMethod` *after* `useValueChanged` reset it to `null`. `lastOpenChangeReason` is sticky (`openChangeReason` is only written by `MenuRoot`'s open-change handler, never by a controlled prop change), so it stays `trigger-press`. Every clause of `initialFocus` is then satisfied on the next programmatic open. Verified in Chromium with the PR's own controlled fixture, using `[MouseLeft>]` → frame → `[/MouseLeft]` for both the opening and closing press: ``` with PR: after programmatic reopen, active role = menu | text = Alpha (the popup) without PR: after programmatic reopen, active role = menuitem | text = More (the trigger) ``` **Failure scenario:** An app drives ``. The user clicks the trigger to open, clicks again to close, then the app reopens the submenu programmatically (state restore, a "reopen last menu" affordance, an undo). Focus jumps off whatever the user was on and onto the submenu popup — the exact behavior the new test at `MenuRoot.test.tsx:104` claims to forbid. That test passes only because `user.click()` dispatches pointerdown/mousedown/mouseup/click in one task, so the rAF close hasn't run yet and `handleTriggerClick` still sees `isOpen === true`. Omitting just the trailing click from my repro restores the correct behavior, isolating it as the cause. **Fix:** Don't rely on `openMethod` as a proxy for "an interaction just opened this". Record the interaction on the open transition itself (or clear `openMethod`/`openChangeReason` when the controlled `open` changes without an event), and change the test to release the press in a separate task so it actually exercises the path. --- ### 3. 🔴 VoiceOver loses `aria-expanded` on a programmatic reopen after a virtual press **Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.tsx:180` ```tsx const focusMovesToSubmenuItem = lastOpenChangeReason === REASONS.listNavigation || openMethod === 'keyboard' || (virtualPress && lastOpenChangeReason === REASONS.triggerPress); ``` This is meant to be the inverse of `MenuPopup`'s condition, but it is missing the `openMethod !== null` clause, and `virtualPress` is never reset while the submenu is open (`!open` guard). So on the stale-state path the popup decides "leave focus on the trigger" while the trigger decides "focus moved to an item" and drops `aria-expanded`. Verified in Chromium (VoiceOver platform mock, virtual press → virtual press to close → `setOpen(true)`): ``` activeElement: More | aria-expanded: null ``` Focus is demonstrably still on the trigger, yet the expanded state is gone. Pre-PR, neither clause matched here, so `aria-expanded="true"` was kept. A second vector for the same drift: `openMethod === 'keyboard'` is not gated by the open reason either, and `openMethod` survives a press whose `onOpenChange` calls `eventDetails.cancel()` (a pattern this PR's own VoiceOver test uses). Enter-with-cancel, then hover to open, also omits `aria-expanded` while focus stays on the trigger. **Failure scenario:** A VoiceOver user opens a controlled submenu with a virtual press, closes it, and the app reopens it. VoiceOver announces "More, menu item" with no expanded state and no submenu content — the user is not told the submenu is open, which is the opposite of what the omission is for. **Fix:** Derive both conditions from one place. See Simplifications #1 — a single `submenuOpenFocus: 'popup' | 'item' | 'trigger'` selector reproduces both and makes this drift unrepresentable. --- ### 4. 🟠 The `aria-expanded` rationale no longer holds for physical presses **Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.tsx:194` ```tsx // Opening a submenu changes the trigger's expanded state while the trigger still holds // focus, and VoiceOver announces that state change instead of the submenu item that focus // moves to a moment later, so the first item is never announced. ``` After this PR a physical pointer press *does* move focus off the trigger — onto the popup — and the new test at `MenuSubmenuTrigger.voiceOver.test.tsx:153` asserts `expect(submenu).toHaveFocus()` two lines before asserting `aria-expanded === 'true'`. If the stated mechanism is real, the expanded-state change should now talk over the menu-container announcement in the same way it talked over the first-item announcement; the predicate that matches the rationale is "focus leaves the trigger" (everything except hover), not `focusMovesToSubmenuItem`. I could not test this — it needs real VoiceOver. Flagging because the mechanism is the one the code itself documents and the scope is narrow but real: macOS VoiceOver + `openOnHover={false}` + trackpad click. **Failure scenario:** VoiceOver user clicks a submenu trigger in an `openOnHover={false}` menu; hears "expanded" instead of the submenu. **Fix:** Confirm on VoiceOver whether the popup announcement survives. If not, widen the omission to every non-hover open. --- ### 5. 🟠 `virtualPress` uses a narrower predicate than floating-ui's own virtual detection **Location:** `packages/react/src/menu/submenu-trigger/MenuSubmenuTrigger.tsx:203` The new flag is set only from `pointerdown`, only via `isVirtualPointerEvent`. floating-ui decides the same thing on the same element from four handlers — `onPointerDown`/`onPointerEnter` via `isVirtualPointerEvent`, and `onMouseDown`/`onClick` via `isVirtualClick` (`useListNavigation.ts:825-836`) — and `isVirtualClick` accepts shapes `isVirtualPointerEvent` rejects (`detail === 0 && !pointerType`, and an Android `click`/`buttons === 1` branch).
